title: Pollution controls left annual thermal transfer at 4 to 8 percent in 217 English river sites
abstract: We tested whether organic pollution explains weak transfer of spatial temperature gradients to annual community change. We used raw ChemPop family-presence records from 217 English river sites: 3,715 autumn samples in 1991-2017 and 79 family labels. We trained multivariate composition axes on 1991-2000 records in one site fold and tested them at held-out sites and in 2001-2017. Held-out spatial slopes were 0.86-0.93. Later within-site temperature slopes were about 0.038, or 4 percent of the spatial slopes. Adjustment for BOD and ammonia in axis training changed little. Survey-day and region-by-year controls gave transfer values of 6-8 percent. Conditional intervals included zero in the main model and excluded zero in the date-controlled models. The primary period did not clearly warm, so its trend ratio did not identify long-term warming debt. The result concerns local annual air-temperature responses and selected autumn family communities. It does not identify a causal equilibrium or the process that sets the long-term gap. Code, aggregate estimates and external-data retrieval instructions are included.
